reason: The guideline-based questions and keeping weight off by default actually speak to me, so I'd download it and use the free first summary. But I'm not paying a period app anything until I've checked that the 'never leaves your phone' claim holds up, and the free tier already covers my next appointment.
objection: Every period app says it's private until it isn't. 'Runs entirely on your phone' is a claim, not a source. I want to see an independent privacy audit or open network traffic before I trust it with fertility data, especially in the US right now.
would_change_my_mind: A published third-party security/privacy audit (or verifiable proof it makes no network calls without the AI toggle), plus the free summary actually getting my reproductive endocrinologist to take my symptoms seriously at the next visit.
